clue.text: The Victoria and Albert isn't able to make admission free

parts.note: the V and A is the usual short name of the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
isn't able means can't, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A London museum is unable to let visitors in for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London. The surface suggests free entry to a museum, but 'free' alone is the definition, in the sense of unoccupied.
explanation.definitionFit: A free seat or room is unoccupied, with nobody in it.

clue.text: Cast given an hour in urban area

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another, here the hour inside the urban area

parts.note: a town is an urban area
hr is the standard abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: An actor's role is handed out with an hour of rehearsal somewhere in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast as a past participle means hurled or tossed, as a stone is.

clue.text: What everyone does in this branch of medicine

definitions.meaning: read literally, the common or usual habit of people at large
the work of a family doctor, who treats all kinds of complaint rather than specialising

explanation.surface: A doctor explains which field of medicine covers what everybody does.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the plain phrase: what is generally practised. The second is the GP's field, the family doctor's surgery work.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary conduct is what is generally done; the family doctor's non-specialist work bears the same name in Britain.

clue.text: They're fabulous feet!

definitions.meaning: myths and fables, stories of the fabulous kind
read as two words, the feet are what lie at the ends of the legs

explanation.surface: An admirer exclaims at a pair of wonderful feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' looks like praise but means 'of fable'. Split the answer as LEG ENDS and you have the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Myths and folk tales are fabulous in the old sense of belonging to fable; the feet terminate each leg.

clue.text: Moderate drivers often get overtaken there

definitions.meaning: an adjective for views that avoid both extremes
the centre lane of a carriageway, where slower motorists are passed

explanation.surface: Sensible motorists are frequently passed by faster traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Political views avoiding extremes are called centrist; the centre lane of a highway is where many slower vehicles get passed.

clue.text: Such a woman is ideally suited to receive the king

indicators.note: to receive means the rearranged letters take in another piece
suited here means fitted or adapted, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A certain kind of woman would make the perfect consort for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suited' rearranges IDEALLY into LADYLIE, and 'to receive' puts K inside it. The definition describes such a woman, so the adjective fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A refined, well-mannered woman is described as genteel or proper in the manner of a lady.

clue.text: Exhausted by the sound of a funeral march

definitions.text: the sound of a funeral march
definitions.meaning: a slow mournful drum rhythm, the beat for the dead

explanation.surface: Someone is worn out by the gloomy tones of a funeral march.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly tired is worn out; a funeral march keeps a slow beat for the departed.

clue.text: Money, and nothing more, gets this wool

parts.note: cash is money
mere means nothing more than, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: Only money buys this fine wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, a luxury fabric.

clue.text: I'm taking a very long time to produce the figures

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
ages means a very long time, as in waiting for ages

explanation.surface: Someone complains of slowness in making some statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures, statues and likenesses are representations of figures.

clue.text: Being supreme

parts.note: read as the Supreme Being, the deity, with the words swapped round; on the surface a description of dominance

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys being on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The Supreme Being is a name for the deity worshipped in monotheistic religions.

clue.text: Petrol acquired only in Georgia and New England

indicators.note: in places the word for only between the two state abbreviations

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
NE is short for New England, the north-eastern US region
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: Fuel is bought only in two American places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the word for only between the two state abbreviations. The definition fits the surface: this is the American spelling of the fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated American spelling of the fuel the British call petrol.

clue.text: Spirits in the wood featured in teetotal commercials

parts.note: dry means alcohol-free, as in a dry county
ads are commercials

explanation.surface: Woodland spirits appear in advertising for alcohol-free drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' tempts toward drink alongside 'teetotal', but here they are tree nymphs.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, tree nymphs inhabit forests and oaks.

clue.text: Dick Turpin's order to the aspiring speaker

definitions.meaning: Dick Turpin was an 18th-century English highwayman, and this was the robber's demand to coach travellers
advice to a would-be politician: put yourself up for election and give your speeches

explanation.surface: A highwayman's demand doubles as advice to a would-be politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The highwayman's traditional demand, and the two tasks of a candidate: offer yourself for election, then make the speeches.

clue.text: Port in Scotland is always right

parts.note: ay is an old poetic word for ever or always

explanation.surface: A Scottish harbour town is forever correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour town on Scotland's south-west coast, also known for its racecourse.

clue.text: Disjointed description of a boxing-match

definitions.meaning: a scrap is a fight, so a fight-filled bout is full of scraps

explanation.surface: A commentator calls a boxing bout disjointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Work made of odd fragments is bitty and uneven; a fist fight is a scrap, so a lively bout is full of them.

clue.text: Salad served as the result of an old monarch's ruling

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme, so his becomes Cole's
a law is a ruling

explanation.surface: A salad is served by decree of a long-dead king.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of an English nursery rhyme; 'old monarch' points at him.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded raw cabbage dressed with mayonnaise is a common side salad.

clue.text: Redolent of a romantic lacking direction

indicators.note: lacking means one letter is dropped from the words before it

parts.note: N for north is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Something smells of a romantic who has lost their way.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means giving off a strong scent, like something fragrant or spicy.

clue.text: The results of having personal property

definitions.meaning: one's belongings, as in a dead person's goods

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the consequences of owning things.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcomes are consequences; one's belongings are called goods or chattels in legal language.

clue.text: Fish from the Cape?

parts.note: the Massachusetts peninsula named after the fish found off its coast; the question mark flags the playful link

explanation.surface: A fish caught off a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A common white food fish, which gave its name to a Massachusetts peninsula.

clue.text: The preparation expected of an orator

definitions.text: The preparation expected of an orator

parts.words: The preparation expected of an orator
parts.note: what a public speaker is expected to have ready: a formal speech

explanation.surface: What a speaker should have ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech delivered to an audience is what an orator prepares.

clue.text: Sensational trademarks of Dracula and Zeus

parts.note: the vampire's trademark is blood
the Greek king of the gods wields thunderbolts

explanation.surface: Two figures of legend have their famous calling cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid melodramatic stories full of violence are described with this phrase.

clue.text: Not a single person is without substance

parts.note: no means without, as in no money
body means substance, as in a wine with body

explanation.surface: Someone says no one is truly insubstantial.
explanation.definitionFit: No one at all, not anyone.

clue.text: I wager eccentric entomologists are familiar with it

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or unusual, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bets that odd insect experts know a certain creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like a description of the entomologists but rearranges I WAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect with pincers at its tail, well known to students of insects.

clue.text: A South German philosopher viewed with suspicion

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
Immanuel Kant was the great German philosopher of Königsberg

explanation.surface: A thinker from southern Germany is regarded with distrust.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking sideways or with distrust; an old variant of askance.

clue.text: One seldom found chicken undercooked?

parts.note: rare meat is lightly cooked
a chicken is a bird

explanation.surface: Underdone chicken is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: An unusual person or thing is likened to an uncommon species of bird.

clue.text: One about to display anger

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to lose their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for wrath.

clue.text: Fellow joins the CIA for a change. He's mad

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: for a change signals the letters of the agency's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man joins the US spy agency to try something new and is thought crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges the agency's three letters. 'Fellow' and 'joins' make the surface read like a news item.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildly mad person, a lunatic.

clue.text: Substitutes tolerate immoral action

parts.note: stand means tolerate, as in can't stand it
a sin is an immoral action

explanation.surface: Replacements put up with wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Replaces someone temporarily, as an understudy does.
